evals.prompt: Generate some sample JSON in C# using Newtonsoft.Json and write it to output.json.
evals.expected_output: Claude writes a single .cs file with a `#:package Newtonsoft.Json` directive at the top, then runs it with `dotnet run <file>.cs`. It does NOT scaffold a project (`dotnet new`, `dotnet add package`), and does NOT generate the JSON inline without executing code. Ideally it cleans up the .cs file afterward.

evals.prompt: Quick one-off: in C#, print the SHA-256 of the string 'hello'. Don't spend time on setup.
evals.expected_output: Claude uses a file-based app (single .cs file, `dotnet run file.cs`) or pipes a one-liner via stdin (`echo '...' | dotnet run -`). It does NOT run `dotnet new console` or create a .csproj — the 'don't spend time on setup' and 'quick one-off' cues should rule out scaffolding.

evals.prompt: Use C# with BenchmarkDotNet to compare two ways of concatenating strings.
evals.expected_output: Claude creates a single .cs file with `#:package BenchmarkDotNet` and runs it via `dotnet run`, rather than scaffolding a console project and adding the package separately. The package is declared with a `#:package` directive, not `dotnet add package`.
